metadata.title: B2: Free Press Accountability
metadata.description: The First Amendment's protection of a free press makes this loop possible. When trust falls, investigative journalists dig harder. Their reporting exposes wrongdoing, prosecutors and Congress hold officials accountable, corruption falls, and trust recovers.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Trust In Government
nodes.description: The percentage of citizens who say they trust the federal government to do what is right most or all of the time.

nodes.label: Investigative Journalism
nodes.description: Reporting that digs beyond official statements — FOIA requests, whistleblower interviews, leaked documents. Watergate is the archetype.

nodes.label: Officials Held Accountable
nodes.description: Resignations, indictments, congressional hearings, and electoral defeats triggered by exposed wrongdoing.

nodes.label: Political Corruption
nodes.description: Bribery, self-dealing, abuse of office, and other betrayals of the public trust.

edges.description: Falling trust drives reader demand for accountability reporting — and motivates reporters to dig.
Exposed wrongdoing prompts prosecutors, ethics committees, and voters to act.
Real consequences for past offenders deter future ones — corruption drops.
Less corruption — and the visible enforcement of consequences — lets trust recover.

loops.label: B2: Free Press Accountability
loops.description: The constitutional check that the Framers built in: a free press that can investigate without government permission.
loops.behavior_pattern: Episodic — works in bursts around major scandals (Watergate, Iran-Contra, Abu Ghraib).
